To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

water soluble phosphorus (TDP) from broiler litter can be underestimated if the conventional extraction procedure is used, that the MES buffer at pH 5.5 is an effective extractant for TDP from broiler litter, and that the amount of TDP released from broiler litter during the incubation can be greater than that removed by the initial extraction.

water extraction of P from broiler litter underestimates P loss in runoff from broiler litter applied to acidic field conditions, but the use of MES buffer to extract P from broiler residue after water extraction may provide a reasonable estimate of the P loss potential of the residue.

water extraction underestimates TDP in broiler litter because the alkalinity in the suspension limits the solu- bility of P compounds, and the amount of TDP released from the litter depends upon the initial P concentration and the pH of the extraction solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of P in the surface soil and thatch after broiler litter is spread on soil and exposed to rainfall.
developing an extraction procedure for determining the water soluble P in broiler litter that will be applicable under field conditions.
the dynamics of P in broiler litter and the effect of water and buffer on the solubility and release of P.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water extraction may underestimate the hazard to water quality, but that the MES buffer may overestimate the hazard.
water extraction of broiler litter is not an appropriate method for determining the amount of P that may be lost in runoff from broiler litter applied to acidic soils.
the MES buffer at pH 5.5 is a better indicator of soluble P in broiler litter than water extraction, but the MES buffer is not a better predictor of P loss in surface runoff.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WER is a better indicator of the hazard of P runoff than the BER, and the MES buffer is a better indicator than water of the amount of P in broiler litter that is available for plant uptake.

the MES buffer at pH 5.6 is more effective than the water extraction procedure at removing TDP from the litter residue and that the MES buffer may be more appropriate than water for estimating the potential for P loss in runoff from litter-applied fields.
the MES buffer at pH 4.5-7.0 is a better extractant than deionized water to determine the hazard of soluble P loss in runoff from surface applied broilers litter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MES buffer at pH 4.6 is an effective extractant to measure the amount of P released by broiler litter during the first 60 d after application, and the amount released is greater than that measured with a conventional water extraction.

water soluble P from broiler litter may be underestimated if water is used to extract P in broiler litter and that a buffer at pH 5 to 6 may be used to more accurately estimate the amount of water soluble P from litter.
the MES buffer at pH 4.5 is a more effective extractant of soluble P from broiler litter than is water.
